findings.title: NPE risk when falling back to the all-clients resource in hasPermission(ClientModel, String)
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which can return null (e.g. when admin permissions are disabled for the realm, or when the type-level resource has not been created). The very next line then calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) with a null resource, which will throw a NullPointerException (or behave unpredictably) instead of returning false. Any admin API call guarded by canManage/canView/canConfigure on a client can therefore fail with a 500 instead of a clean authorization denial.

findings.title: Per-client resource shadows the all-clients permission fallback
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only falls back to the type-level 'Clients' resource when resourceStore.findByName returns null for the client's own resource. If a per-client resource exists (e.g. created earlier by a view-only permission) but no permission on it grants the requested scope, the type-level (all clients) permission is never evaluated. An admin who was granted 'manage' on all clients would then be denied manage on that specific client simply because some other, narrower permission once referenced it. The two levels should both be evaluated (or the evaluation should check type-level permissions regardless).

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission finds no per-client resources and leaks the type-level resource name
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission lists resources via resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...). However, per-client resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId()) without setting a type, so they are not returned by a type query; the only resource that carries type 'Clients' is the type-level resource created in init(). Consequently the method (a) fails to return the IDs of clients that have per-client permissions granted, and (b) adds the name 'Clients' (the type-level resource name, not a client ID) to the result set when a type-level permission matches, which consumers will treat as a client ID. Either set the resource type when creating per-client resources, or query by name and filter out the type-level resource.

findings.title: Client-removed listener can throw UnsupportedOperationException when V2 feature is enabled
findings.body: registerListener now gates the event handling on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) and then calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). But management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 (and thus ClientPermissionsV2) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported in V2'). When both features are enabled (V2 is a preview feature that can coexist with V1), deleting any client (or removing a role/group) will trigger this listener and throw an UnsupportedOperationException inside the removal flow, breaking client/role/group deletion.

findings.title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext is unused and canExchangeTo is unimplemented
findings.body: The private method getEvaluationContext (lines 262-272) is never referenced anywhere in the class; it appears to be a leftover from token-exchange support. Together with the unused imports (Scope, EvaluationContext, TOKEN_EXCHANGE constant, and the unused logger), it suggests token-exchange evaluation was intended but canExchangeTo just throws UnsupportedOperationException. If token exchange for clients is not supported in V2 yet, the dead code should be removed; if it was intended to work, canExchangeTo throwing UnsupportedOperationException is a functional regression versus V1 for realms that enable the V2 feature.
